brewing.notes: A safe starting point for raw pu-erh: rinse once, gongfu style, short early steeps.

description:
A seed-propagated, tree-type, late-budding large-leaf tea plant native to Mangang village in Bangdong, Lincang.

This is a tea plant cultivar rather than a finished tea, so you are more likely to meet its name in a grower's notes than on a packet. If you find tea made from it, brew it like any other raw pu-erh tea and taste what the plant brings.
history: Left to grow, the plant can reach 9.3 metres with a spread of 7.8 metres. Its very large elliptical leaves are deep green, glossy, thick and soft, and its stout green buds are heavily downy. Little more is documented about it.
processing: A plant cultivar, not a processing style: it is usually made into raw pu-erh tea, and the method is up to the grower.
harvest_season: Depends on the place and the grower.
appearance_dry: Depends on how the leaf is processed.
appearance_liquor: Depends on how the leaf is processed.
appearance_wet: Depends on how the leaf is processed.
taste_profile: Depends on how the leaf is processed; tea from it usually falls within what raw pu-erh teas give.
vintage_note: A cultivar is not sold by vintage. Tea made from it follows the usual pattern for raw pu-erh tea, so ask for the harvest year and the grower.
